# Readiness gap delta — #330

Status: complete, report only; no repository files changed. The original 31-row table is available in [the staged #282 report](exports/reports/282.json). This table preserves its order and adds the two requested rows. Review outcomes below are attributed to current main's status record, not independently revalidated against case/result bodies.

The remaining blockers are **not only resources**: public lineage adjudication, manifest-content binding and a populated-manifest/runner validation contract remain public work. Sources/tasks/oracle/coverage are now `reviewed`, within their limited public provenance/XML-key/native-design scope; #212 disclosure and #281 checker findings are closed by #298/#300. Native and baseline execution remain absent, all 23 native slots unresolved, and quality unmeasured ([preparation-status.json:11–25](../benchmark/preparation-status.json)).

The owner must accept a credible, independently checked verification method and its pinned evidence before implementation: evaluation.md:14–15 says “dopuszcza rozpoczęcie implementacji dopiero po wiarygodnej metodzie weryfikacji”; :58–59 requires independent verification and says “Nie wystarczy utworzyć pliki.” [Protocol.md:129](../benchmark/protocol.md) explicitly says “prepare substantive development evidence, independently checked keys, tested split isolation and executed challenges” and then “Pin evidence and obtain owner acceptance of the verification method before product implementation.” Thus native evidence sufficient to establish the semantic keys/challenges, and executed split-isolation evidence, cannot all be deferred to later readiness under the current protocol. A completed matched product baseline is not explicitly required before method acceptance: its execution belongs to benchmark comparison/readiness, while its repeatable procedure must be credible and reviewed. The native capability itself requires an end-to-end job, not compile success (protocol.md:120). The owner can decide a staged method acceptance, but treating all execution as later readiness would require an explicit protocol/acceptance decision, not this audit's reinterpretation. Quality thresholds, scope/fallback and final goal gate remain separate owner decisions ([evaluation.md:18–22](../docs/perpetua/evaluation.md); [goal.md:18–20](../goal/goal.md)).

| #282 requirement | Current main and evidence pointer | Class / remaining action |

| 6. Sources provenance and environments | Sources now reviewed; #288 provenance/header scope excludes native semantics (preparation-status.json:17,23; sources.md:49). | done for public preparation review; native dependency/read-version evidence remains resource-dependent #169. |
| 7. Task families, keys and original locators | Tasks now reviewed within XML-key/native-design scope; 11 cases/four families, 23 unresolved native slots (preparation-status.json:3–16,25). | resource-dependent #169/#268 for semantic and restricted cases; public XML review is done. |

| 29. Model access, runner and quota | Provider/model/recipients/quota undecided; synthetic records do not verify accounting or routing (baseline/README.md:7,25,33). | owner-decision for concrete selections/quota; runner validation design is now-doable N3. |
| 30. Independent reviewers/checkers and scoring authority | Scoped public reviews landed; no complete native key/method acceptance, and model-family uncertainty remains (preparation-status.json:16–17; protocol.md:125). | resource-dependent #169/#268 for substantive evidence review; Policymaker can order separate public reviews of N1–N3 now. |
| 31. Concrete proposals, pinned evidence and owner decisions | Public reviews improved; protocol still requires checked keys, tested isolation and executed challenges before method acceptance (protocol.md:128–130). | owner-decision for acceptance/provisioning; N1–N3 and #169/#268 prerequisites remain. |
| 32. #318 finding 4: manifest-content binding | `run_record.py:134–135` checks hash shape, not equality to supplied manifest bytes; README explicitly retains binding and negative test before runner integration (baseline/README.md:33). | now-doable N1. |
| 33. Public lineage adjudication | 230 overlapping candidate groups / 1,244 different-hash pairs remain unadjudicated; only conservative grouping exists (lineage.md:10–21). | now-doable N2 for public non-native adjudication; native structural uncertainty remains resource-dependent #169. |

Each now-doable row refers to a bounded task below; these tasks prepare evidence and do not establish native answers, isolation or a completed benchmark.

| ID | One-sentence task and files touched | Pinned-file consequence |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | Bind a synthetic run record's manifest hash to explicitly defined supplied manifest bytes, add a wrong-content/valid-hash negative control, and obtain separate review before runner integration; touch `benchmark/scripts/run_record.py`, `benchmark/baseline/README.md`, and the run-record template if its contract changes. | All named existing files are pinned: re-pin each changed entry in `benchmark/preparation.json` and run the index check. |
| N2 | Adjudicate public lineage candidates from preserved provenance/XML/hash evidence, retaining unresolved native relationships conservatively and requesting independent review; touch `benchmark/scripts/lineage.py`, `benchmark/lineage.json`, `benchmark/lineage.md`, and status only if supported by review. | These existing files are pinned: update every changed hash in `benchmark/preparation.json`; keep each evidence file under 2 MB. |
| N3 | Specify and independently review populated-manifest validation plus a repeatable paired-runner contract covering unresolved record mappings, interruptions, raw preservation and N1 binding, while leaving resource choices and executions explicitly unavailable; touch `benchmark/baseline/README.md`, add a distinct populated-manifest/runner contract under `benchmark/baseline/`, and add a separate validator under `benchmark/scripts/` if ordered. | README is pinned and must be re-pinned; new milestone evidence must be indexed with hashes, without relaxing the existing undecided-template checker or changing evaluator policy. |

Verification: `python3 -I -B benchmark/scripts/score.py --check` exited 0: `{"cannot_evaluate":0,"controls":33,"fixtures":3,"matches":33,"mismatches":0}`. `python3 -I -B policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check` exited 0: `errors: []`, `missing: []`, 62 references, `benchmark_ready: false`, `benchmark_executed: false`, `tool_quality: null`. `run_record.py --check` also exited 0 with design_only true, runs 0 and six rejected mutations; none tests manifest-content binding. These are environment-free checks, not native executions or measured quality. No development-case or results JSON body was opened. Working tree was clean at the final inspection.

## What next

Saved work is this report only. Policymaker should order N1–N3 with separate substantive reviews while the owner advances #169/#268, including the #327 store rerun. Then collect/review the development/native challenge and split-isolation evidence required by protocol.md:129 before submitting an unconditional owner method-acceptance request; explicitly identify any requested staged exception. The next cold session should use this delta and current status, avoid repeating closed XML/disclosure/checker reviews or the integrity-only audit, and never substitute milestone labels or synthetic controls for missing native coverage and unmeasured tool quality.

decision: do-first N1,N2,N3 — non-resource preparation remains, and the current protocol additionally requires substantive checked development evidence, tested split isolation and executed challenges before unconditional method acceptance.

No changes to merge.
